chunks: your son gave you happiness while, at the same time, he was a trial and hardship, and he grieved you while, at the same time, he has proved a source of reward and mercy for you.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of a child being both a trial and a source of mercy?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha, this saying encapsulates the Shia concept of *fitnah* (trial) and *ibtila* (testing) inherent in familial bonds, where the beloved child serves as both a source of worldly attachment and a means of spiritual purification. The duality reflects the belief that grief is not merely a loss but a transformative state leading to *thawab* (reward) and *rahmah* (mercy), aligning with the Imams' teaching that endurance in affliction elevates one's rank in the Hereafter.

en.sayed-ali-raza: your son (when he lived) gave you happiness while, at the same time, he was a trial and hardship and (when he died) he grieved you while, at the same time, he has proved a source of reward and mercy for you.
